planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in fall into well-drained soil in full sun; Golden Rose of China is an early-spring bloomer with fern-like, finely divided foliage.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; Golden Rose of China is a classic wild species, long cultivated in China and Korea, bearing bright yellow single to semi-double flowers about 2 inches across in early spring on an arching shrub 6-8 feet tall. Its fern-like, finely divided foliage distinguishes it visually from other yellow-flowered species roses even before it blooms. It has served as a parent species behind many yellow-flowered rose hybrids and tolerates a range of garden conditions once established.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in fall into well-drained soil in full sun; Golden Rose of Afghanistan is among the hardiest and earliest-blooming species roses.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; Golden Rose of Afghanistan is a compact species rose reaching 3-4 feet, with tiny fern-like leaflets and small, bright buttercup-yellow flowers about an inch across opening very early in spring. It is among the hardiest and earliest-blooming species roses in cultivation and has been used as a breeding parent for hardy yellow hybrid roses. Its small scale and fine texture suit a rock garden or species-rose collection rather than a conventional shrub border.

subcategory: species shrub rose grown for hips

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in fall into well-drained soil in full sun; Himalayan Musk-Briar is valued for its glaucous blue-gray foliage as much as its flowers.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; Himalayan Musk-Briar is a high-altitude species rose with distinctive glaucous blue-gray foliage, pale pink single flowers, and showy bottle-shaped orange-red hips that persist into autumn. Reaching about 6 feet, it is valued as much for its foliage color and ornamental hips as for its modest bloom display. It tolerates cold, exposed conditions reflecting its high-elevation Himalayan origin.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in fall against a sturdy support in full sun; Soulie's Rose is a vigorous rambler, the ancestor of 'Kew Rambler' and other garden hybrids.

directions: Plant against a sturdy pergola, fence, or large shrub in full sun in well-drained soil; Soulie's Rose is a vigorous Chinese rambling species with gray-green foliage, bearing large clusters of creamy-white, fragrant flowers in summer. It can reach 10-15 feet as a climber or scrambler and is notably drought-tolerant once established, a genuine advantage over many less drought-hardy climbing roses. It is a well-known rambler parent, having contributed to garden hybrids such as 'Kew Rambler.'

subcategory: species shrub rose grown for hips

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in fall into well-drained soil in full sun; Sweginzow's Rose is grown primarily for its spectacular ornamental hips rather than its bloom.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; Sweginzow's Rose is a Chinese species rose bearing clear pink single flowers in early summer, followed by large, spectacular flask- or bottle-shaped orange-red hips that persist well into winter, the main reason this upright 8-10 foot shrub is grown. It is a favorite among collectors seeking strong autumn and winter hip display rather than a long bloom season, and is hardy well into cold continental climates.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in fall into moist, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Cluster Rose is native to Pacific Northwest wet meadows and streambanks.

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade in moist, well-drained soil; Cluster Rose is a clump-forming native of wet meadows and streambanks ranging from British Columbia to California, bearing clusters of small pink flowers in late spring and summer followed by small round red hips. Reaching 3-6 feet, it is a useful native and pollinator planting for a rain garden or stream-margin restoration where a true wild rose species fits the ecological planting goal better than a hybrid cultivar.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in fall against a sturdy support or into a mature tree in full sun; Rosa longicuspis is extremely vigorous and needs ample room to climb.

directions: Plant against a sturdy support or an established tree in full sun; Rosa longicuspis is an extremely vigorous Himalayan and Chinese rambler, closely related to the already-grown Rosa mulligani but sold and grown as a distinct accession, bearing glossy foliage and large trusses of small, fragrant white single flowers in summer. It is famously grown at Sissinghurst Castle's White Garden, climbing 20 feet or more into supporting trees. Give it ample room and a sturdy host, since it will quickly overwhelm a small trellis.

planting.note: Plant container stock in fall into lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Baja California Rose is a rare chaparral endemic suited to a xeriscape or native collector garden.

directions: Plant in full sun in lean, well-drained soil; Baja California Rose is a diminutive, densely branched, very drought-tolerant chaparral endemic from Baja California and southernmost San Diego County, with some of the smallest leaflets of any rose species and small pink flowers. Reaching only 1-3 feet, it suits a xeriscape planting or a dedicated native/species rose collector's garden rather than a conventional rose bed. It is only occasionally offered by California native-plant specialty growers, so sourcing requires some searching.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in fall into well-drained soil in full sun; Dahurian Rose is exceptionally cold-hardy, valued in breeding programs for extreme winter survival.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; Dahurian Rose is an exceptionally cold-hardy East Asian and Siberian species rose, bearing pink single flowers in early summer, small red hips, and fine-textured foliage. Native from Siberia through Manchuria and Korea, it is valued in cold-climate breeding programs for its extreme winter hardiness, surviving zone 2-3 conditions that few other roses tolerate. It is less common in general retail trade than Rosa rugosa but is genuinely cultivated in northern botanic garden and arboretum collections.
